proposed_comments.title: Add behavioral coverage for shelf shortcut and context-menu routing
proposed_comments.body:
### Add behavioral coverage for shelf shortcut and context-menu routing

**Severity:** `medium`

This PR adds a new focused-shelf keyboard path that handles Ctrl+Enter, Ctrl+K, requested context-menu shortcuts, asynchronous context hydration, and submenu/flyout lifecycle, but the new tests only verify which model gets wrapped for a shelf item. Please add CmdPal UI tests under `src/modules/cmdpal/Tests/Microsoft.CmdPal.UITests` that focus a quick-access shelf item and verify the new user-visible behaviors: Ctrl+Enter invokes the shelf item's secondary command, Ctrl+K opens the shelf context menu, a requested shortcut routes through `QuickAccessShelfContextControl.TryInvokeKeybinding`, and a shortcut that targets a submenu leaves the context menu open at that submenu.

The existing `CommandPaletteTestBase.OpenContextMenu()` and `IndexerTests` context-menu tests are good patterns for locating menu entries and asserting behavior. The key point is to exercise `TryHandleQuickAccessShelfItemKeyDown` through the UI, not just `QuickAccessShelfItem.GetContextMenuItem()`, so regressions in focus, timing, or flyout reopen/cleanup behavior are caught before merge.

confidence.rationale: The change adds substantial user-visible UI routing while the new tests cover only model wrapping; existing CmdPal UI-test patterns can exercise the behavior.
